lines.text: Why do you scar now? Before birth, a cut healed without one.
lines.phonemes: wˌaɪ dˈuː juː skˈɑː nˈaʊ? bɪfˌɔː bˈɜːθ, ɐ kˈʌt hˈiːld wɪðˈaʊt wˌɒn.

lines.text: Under the surface, most of your skin's strength is collagen, woven every which way like a basket, so it gives whichever way it's pulled.
lines.phonemes: ˌʌndə ðə sˈɜːfɪs, mˈəʊst əv jɔː skˈɪnz stɹˈɛŋθ ɪz kˈɒləʤən , wˈəʊvən ˈɛvɹɪ wˌɪtʃ wˈeɪ lˈaɪk ɐ bˈaskɪt, sˌəʊ ɪt ɡˈɪvz wɪtʃˈɛvə wˈeɪ ɪts pˈʊld.

lines.text: Cut through it, and the body doesn't reweave. It patches: new threads side by side, all one way, with no hair or sweat glands.
lines.phonemes: kˈʌt θɹˈuː ɪt, and ðə bˈɒdi dˈʌzənt ɹɪwˈiːv. ɪt pˈatʃɪz: njˈuː θɹˈɛdz sˈaɪd baɪ sˈaɪd, ˈɔːl wˈɒn wˈeɪ, wɪð nˈəʊ hˈeə ɔː swˈɛt ɡlˈandz.

lines.text: We call that healed, as good as new. But pulled until it tears, even an old scar is only as strong as a rope missing one strand in five.
lines.phonemes: wiː kˈɔːl ðat hˈiːld, az ɡˈʊd az njˈuː. bˌʌt pˈʊld ʌntˈɪl ɪt tˈeəz, ˈiːvən ɐn ˈəʊld skˈɑːɹ ɪz ˈəʊnli az stɹˈɒŋ az ɐ ɹˈəʊp mˈɪsɪŋ wˈɒn stɹˈand ɪn fˈaɪv.

lines.text: Until about the sixth month of pregnancy, a baby's skin regrows the weave, follicles and all. And one place in you still nearly can: your mouth.
lines.phonemes: ʌntˈɪl ɐbˌaʊt ðə sˈɪksθ mˈʌnθ ɒv pɹˈɛɡnənsi, ɐ bˈeɪbiz skˈɪn ɹɪɡɹˈəʊz ðə wˈiːv, fˈɒlɪkəlz and ˈɔːl. and wˈɒn plˈeɪs ɪn juː stˈɪl nˌiəli kˈan: jɔː mˈaʊθ.

lines.text: But on most of your body, only the top layer, about this paper's thickness, regrows without a seam.
lines.phonemes: bˌʌt ˌɒn mˈəʊst əv jɔː bˈɒdi, ˈəʊnli ðə tˈɒp lˈeɪə, ɐbˌaʊt ðɪs pˈeɪpəz θˈɪknəs, ɹɪɡɹˈəʊz wɪðˌaʊt ɐ sˈiːm.

lines.text: So, why the scar? Mice born without germ-fighting cells heal without one: a scar may be the price of defence.
lines.phonemes: sˈəʊ, wˌaɪ ðə skˈɑː? mˈaɪs bˈɔːn wɪðˌaʊt dʒˈɜːmfˈaɪtɪŋ sˈɛlz hˈiːl wɪðˈaʊt wˌɒn: ɐ skˈɑː mˈeɪ biː ðə pɹˈaɪs ɒv dɪfˈɛns.

lines.text: Next: a deadly poison, in a frown. How much goes in?
lines.phonemes: nˈɛkst: ɐ dˈɛdli pˈɔɪzən, ɪn ɐ fɹˈaʊn. hˌaʊ mˈʌtʃ ɡəʊz ˈɪn?
